methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $129M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Candela is a Series C transportation technology company founded by Gustav Hasselskog that has raised €129M to date. The transportation sector contains seven private comparables (including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia) and no public peers, limiting traditional benchmarking.

Valuation analysis relies primarily on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the €129M total capital raised proxy. This approach yields an implied valuation of $219M. A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within transportation; the narrow peer set lacks the three or more datapoints required for reliable median-based triangulation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given sector-specific capital intensity and development timelines.

The single-method triangulation produces a median valuation of $219M, with a low of $186M (15% haircut) and a high of $252M (15% upside), reflecting parameter uncertainty around stage-typical multipliers and the representativeness of raised capital as a valuation proxy. Primary uncertainties center on the applicability of 1.7x advancement multiples to frontier transportation, the absence of comparable Series C exit data in this sector, and the limited visibility into Candela's unit economics and pathway to revenue inflection relative to peer benchmarks.
